intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A must-do eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species including the great green macaw. Between July and October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Jungle Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike concludes at a stunning Pacific Ocean beach, perfect for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk a series of hanging suspension bridges through primary rainforest in the shadow of the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting wildlife at every level of the forest canopy. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush jungle — the ultimate eco-adventure reward.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unparalleled chances to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their pristine natural habitat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange a small amount of cash at the airport (use ATMs for better rates). Take a budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with the hotel surroundings and nearby beach.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely sunset stroll along the beachfront. Explore the immediate area around the resort, locate nearby sodas (local Costa Rican eateries) and budget supermarkets for snacks and water.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for a local soda or sandwich counter (approx. $5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby local soda — try a Casado (rice, beans, salad, protein) for $6–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a local SIM card at the airport (Kolbi or Claro) for affordable data. Download offline maps of Costa Rica. Keep arrival day relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and nearby mangroves. Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, and tropical birds at dawn — completely free. Bring water and wear light layers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest national park or wildlife reserve accessible from the resort. Explore trails on foot or rent a bicycle from a local shop ($10–15/day). Look for sloths, toucans, and scarlet macaws.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Attend a free or low-cost local cultural event if available, or relax on the beach watching for bioluminescence in the water.

meals.breakfast: Buy fresh fruit, bread, and juice from a local market or supermarket ($3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside soda near the park — rice and beans with chicken or fish ($5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from a local supermarket, or eat at a budget soda near the resort ($6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny weather and warm temperatures. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and carry insect repellent on all nature walks.

day_by_day.morning: Join a shared group zip-lining tour booked through a local operator (look for deals at $40–60 USD for group rates). Many operators near beach towns offer early morning departure slots with transport included.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole for a refreshing dip. Ask locals or your hotel for the closest free or low-entry-fee spots.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby town's central market or street food scene. Try local snacks like empanadas, patacones, and fresh coconut water.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda — the classic Costa Rican breakfast ($3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the supermarket to eat near the waterfall — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks ($4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food at the local market — try chifrijo or a fish taco ($5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance or the evening before to secure group pricing. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. Bring a dry bag for valuables near the waterfall.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided bird-watching walk at sunrise along the coastline or forest edge near the resort. Costa Rica is home to over 900 bird species — February is an excellent birding month.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife sanctuary or rescue center (entry typically $15–25 USD). Interact with rescued sloths, monkeys, and exotic birds while supporting conservation efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga or meditation on the beach (many resorts offer free or low-cost sessions). Alternatively, journal your wildlife encounters and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh tropical fruit plate from a beach café ($4–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Casado at a local soda near the wildlife sanctuary ($6–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget beachfront restaurant — grilled fish of the day with rice and salad ($10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wildlife sanctuaries often require advance booking. Avoid any tourist traps that allow harmful animal interactions — choose certified, ethical sanctuaries only.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion begins: Take a shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby national park (e.g., Manuel Antonio, Tortuguero, or Corcovado depending on resort location). Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike national park trails with a free or low-cost park map. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, sloths, and colorful poison dart frogs. Swim at a designated beach within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Rest and rehydrate. Enjoy a quiet evening on the resort's beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda before departure ($3–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the supermarket eaten inside the park — no food vendors inside many parks ($4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — try whole fried red snapper (pargo entero) ($12–16 USD)

day_by_day.notes: National park entry fees typically range from $18–20 USD per person. Book tickets online in advance as parks like Manuel Antonio have daily visitor caps. Wear waterproof hiking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, then enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend time at the resort beach — snorkel, swim, or simply relax. Rent snorkel gear locally ($5–10 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town on foot or by bicycle. Visit a local artisan market to find affordable handmade souvenirs — hammocks, painted gourds, and coffee. Practice bargaining respectfully.
day_by_day.evening: Join a guided night wildlife tour ($20–35 USD through a local operator). Spot nocturnal creatures like tree frogs, bats, caimans, and owls with a knowledgeable guide.

meals.breakfast: Homemade breakfast — buy eggs, bread, and local cheese from the supermarket and cook in resort kitchen if available ($2–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside soda — fresh ceviche and plantains ($7–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the night tour — rice bowl or wrap from a local spot ($5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Night tours are magical and highly recommended. Wear long sleeves and pants, and bring insect repellent. Most tours last 2–3 hours and include a flashlight.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a white-water rafting or river kayaking excursion (shared group tours range $45–65 USD). Many operators offer transport from beach towns to nearby rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, visit a local coffee or chocolate farm tour ($15–25 USD). Learn about Costa Rica's famous cacao and coffee production and enjoy tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening — beach bonfire if permitted, or stargazing away from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with fresh orange juice at a local soda ($4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch included with many rafting tours, or grab a soda meal nearby ($6–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook at the resort or buy a rotisserie chicken with sides from a local market ($6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting difficulty varies by river — Class II–III is ideal for beginners. All gear is provided. The chocolate farm tour is a unique, educational, and delicious experience worth the cost.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby sea turtle nesting or hatching site (seasonal — February may offer sightings depending on location). Join a certified eco-tour to protect the turtles while observing responsibly ($25–40 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore tide pools along the rocky coastline near the resort. Discover starfish, sea urchins, crabs, and small fish in natural pools — completely free and fascinating.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local community event, live music performance, or cultural dance show if available in the nearby town. Ask your hotel concierge for free or low-cost events.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and granola from a beach café ($4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside soda — try a traditional olla de carne (beef stew) or sopa negra (black bean soup) ($5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget-friendly international restaurant for a change of pace ($8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle tours must be booked through licensed operators to ensure ethical practices. Flash photography is strictly prohibited near turtles. February is leatherback nesting season on some coasts.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day guided eco-hike through a private rainforest reserve ($20–35 USD). Learn about medicinal plants, tropical trees, and the rainforest ecosystem from a local naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon at the beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding or boogie boarding — rent boards locally ($10–15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a budget meal together using local ingredients. Visit the nearest farmers' market or pulpería (corner store) for fresh vegetables, rice, beans, and local spices.

meals.breakfast: Pinto breakfast at a soda — eggs, gallo pinto, toast, and natilla (sour cream) ($4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks for the hike — granola bars, bananas, and water ($2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal using local ingredients — rice, beans, plantains, and grilled chicken ($4–7 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: Private rainforest reserves often offer more intimate wildlife encounters than crowded national parks. Ask your guide about the best spots for spotting sloths and poison dart frogs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby volcano or hot springs (budget option: look for free or low-cost natural hot springs rather than resort pools). Travel by local bus to save money.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike volcano trails or explore the volcanic landscape. Many active and dormant volcanoes in Costa Rica have accessible viewpoints and lava fields worth exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural hot springs (free natural springs exist near many volcanoes — ask locals for directions). Return to resort by evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a soda before the bus departure ($3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Soda near the volcano area — typical Tico lunch plate ($6–9 USD)
meals.dinner: Late dinner back at the resort area — try arroz con pollo (chicken and rice) at a local soda ($6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Local buses are extremely affordable ($2–5 USD per leg) but slower than shuttles. Check bus schedules the day before. Bring layers as volcano areas can be cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Morning canopy tour or aerial tram through the rainforest ($35–55 USD for group rates). Experience the treetop ecosystem from above and spot birds and monkeys in the canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a butterfly garden or insect museum near the resort area ($10–15 USD). Learn about Costa Rica's incredible biodiversity including morpho butterflies and leaf-cutter ants.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer local seafood restaurant. Try lobster, shrimp, or fresh catch of the day as a trip highlight meal.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit plate with yogurt and granola at a beach café ($5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the butterfly garden café or a nearby soda ($5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant — splurge night ($15–22 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Aerial trams provide a gentler alternative to zip-lining and are excellent for wildlife spotting. Book in advance. The butterfly garden is a great educational stop and photography opportunity.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife morning — take one last sunrise walk along the beach or forest trail. Review your wildlife journal and photograph any missed species. Visit a local lookout point for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping at the local artisan market — pick up coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and handmade crafts as gifts. Budget $20–40 USD for quality souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Pack bags and prepare for departure. Reflect on the trip over a final quiet dinner. Share photos and memories with fellow travelers met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Full Costa Rican breakfast at a favorite soda discovered during the trip ($4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the market while shopping — try empanadas and fresh juice ($4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a beloved local soda — order your favorite dish from the trip ($7–11 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm your departure transfer or shuttle for Day 13. Pack wildlife field guides or postcards as meaningful budget souvenirs. Leave a review for local guides and sodas that provided great service.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort — enjoy one last swim or beach walk at sunrise. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transport to the airport well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow 3+ hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Costa Rican coffee or chocolate purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of eco-adventures, wildlife encounters, and zip-lining through the rainforest canopy.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda ($3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — budget $8–12 USD for a meal before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snacks

day_by_day.notes: Shared shuttles to the airport cost $20–35 USD and are the most budget-friendly option. Book 24–48 hours in advance. Keep $29 USD cash available if airport exit tax is not included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it). Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A must-do eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Jungle Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike concludes at a stunning Pacific Ocean beach, perfect for a refreshing swim.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to the Aegean Bliss Resort on the Pacific coast (approx. 2.5–3 hr drive depending on location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort, check in, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach to orient yourself, breathe in the ocean air, and watch for brown pelicans and frigatebirds soaring overhead. Pick up a resort map and plan the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Watch the famous Costa Rican Pacific sunset from the terrace before retiring early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or coffee at the airport before boarding or upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick 'casado' (rice, beans, protein) at a roadside 'soda' (local diner) during the transfer drive — budget-friendly and authentically Costa Rican
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — order fresh grilled fish of the day with patacones (fried plantains) and a local Imperial or Pilsen beer (~$20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance. Exchange some currency to Costa Rican Colones (CRC) at the airport for small purchases. Keep luggage light for easy transfer. February is dry season on the Pacific — expect warm, sunny weather around 28–32°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk on the resort grounds and nearby beach at sunrise (6:00–7:30 AM). February dry season means excellent wildlife visibility. Look for scarlet macaws, howler monkeys in the trees, and marine iguanas near the shore. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided kayak and snorkeling tour departing from the resort beach (approx. 3 hours, ~$45–60 per person). Paddle through calm Pacific waters, explore rocky outcroppings teeming with marine life, and snorkel among colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and starfish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a fresh shower, then head into the nearest town for dinner at a local 'soda' restaurant. Explore the town's small artisan market for handmade souvenirs and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort buffet or à la carte — gallo pinto (rice and beans with eggs), fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee (~$10–15)
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack provided by the tour or stop at a beachside kiosk for fresh coconut water and ceviche (~$5–10)
meals.dinner: Local 'soda' in town — try 'olla de carne' (beef and vegetable stew) or fresh grilled snapper with rice and salad (~$8–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak/snorkel tour through the resort activities desk upon arrival on Day 1. Wear reef-safe sunscreen only. Bring a dry bag for electronics during water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Jungle Hike (featured experience) — depart early at 7:00 AM with a certified naturalist guide. Spend 3–4 hours exploring Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, poison dart frogs, and hundreds of bird species including toucans and motmots.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, enjoy free time on Manuel Antonio's famous white-sand beach inside the park (one of the most beautiful in Central America). Swim in calm turquoise waters, relax under a palm tree, and keep an eye out for coatis and squirrel monkeys on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort area and stop for dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Quepos or nearby town, known for excellent fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee (pack a banana and granola bar for the trail)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the park beach or at the park's designated eating area — purchase from a local vendor outside the park entrance (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Mid-range seafood restaurant in Quepos — try 'corvina al ajillo' (garlic sea bass) with yuca fries and a fresh fruit smoothie (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitors — book guided hike tickets at least 2–3 days in advance online. Park opens at 7:00 AM; early entry is best for wildlife sightings. Wear neutral-colored lightweight clothing, closed-toe shoes, and bring insect repellent. The park is about 30–45 minutes from most Pacific coast resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding tour through coastal rainforest and to a hidden waterfall (approx. 3 hours, ~$55–75 per person). Ride through secondary forest trails, cross small streams, and arrive at a secluded waterfall where you can swim in a natural pool. A fantastic eco-adventure with scenic wildlife spotting along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for lunch and a relaxed afternoon. Spend time at the resort pool or beach. Optional: take a beginner surfing lesson on the resort beach with a local instructor (~$40–50 for 1.5 hrs including board rental) — February's dry season brings consistent, beginner-friendly waves.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's beach bar, followed by a cooking class or dinner at a farm-to-table restaurant nearby that sources ingredients from local organic farms.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Costa Rican spread with gallo pinto, fresh juice, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — fish tacos, a fresh salad, and agua de pipa (coconut water) (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table restaurant near the resort — seasonal tasting menu with local ingredients like heart of palm, plantain, and sustainably caught fish (~$20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the horseback riding tour through the resort or a local operator the day before. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes for riding. Bring a change of clothes if you plan to swim at the waterfall. Surfing lessons are typically offered in the morning and late afternoon — confirm timing with the instructor.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird-watching tour with a local ornithologist guide (6:00–9:00 AM, ~$35–50 per person). February is excellent for birding on the Pacific coast. Target species include scarlet macaws, resplendent quetzals (if at higher elevation), trogons, kingfishers, and over 50 other species in just a few hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: arrange a private shuttle or shared shuttle transfer to Monteverde (approx. 4–5 hours via scenic mountain road). Arrive in the cooler cloud forest town of Monteverde/Santa Elena in the late afternoon. Check into a mid-range eco-lodge or boutique hotel in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Santa Elena on foot. Browse local artisan shops, visit a local chocolate or coffee shop for a tasting, and enjoy the cool mountain air (Monteverde sits at ~1,440 m elevation — bring a light jacket).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before the bird-watching tour — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Stop at a local 'soda' along the transfer route — classic casado with chicken or fish (~$7–10)
meals.dinner: Charming restaurant in Santa Elena — try 'picadillo de papa' (potato hash with beef) or vegetarian hearts of palm stew, with local craft beer (~$12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from the Pacific coast to Monteverde involves winding mountain roads — bring motion sickness medication if needed. The road to Monteverde is unpaved in sections; a 4WD vehicle is recommended. Pack a light jacket or fleece as temperatures in Monteverde range from 15–22°C. Book Monteverde accommodation in advance as it's a popular destination.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour (featured experience) — the highlight of the trip! Depart at 8:00 AM for one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits soaring through misty cloud forest canopy. Experience multiple cables (some over 1 km long), Tarzan swings, and hanging bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. Duration: approx. 3–4 hours (~$60–80 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon walk (2–3 hours, ~$25 entrance fee). Walk through mystical cloud forest draped in bromeliads, orchids, and mosses. Look for resplendent quetzals (February is nesting season!), three-wattled bellbirds, and glass frogs.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with a naturalist guide (approx. 2 hours, ~$25–35 per person). Discover the nocturnal world of the cloud forest — spot sleeping birds, tree frogs, walking stick insects, tarantulas, and kinkajous by flashlight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Monteverde eco-lodge — typical Costa Rican breakfast with eggs, gallo pinto, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Café or restaurant near the zip-line or reserve entrance — fresh soup, sandwich, and tropical fruit juice (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Monteverde's popular mid-range restaurant — try wood-fired pizza or pasta with local mushrooms and cheese, plus a glass of Costa Rican guaro sour (~$14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes you don't mind getting muddy for both the zip-line and forest walks. Gloves are provided for zip-lining. The cloud forest is often misty and cool — layer up. Book the night walk in advance through your lodge or the reserve directly. February is dry season at lower elevations but Monteverde's cloud forest maintains its misty character year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Curi-Cancha Wildlife Reserve (a quieter alternative to the main reserve, ~$20 entrance). Spend 2–3 hours walking well-maintained trails with excellent wildlife viewing. Curi-Cancha is renowned for reliable quetzal sightings and is less crowded than the main reserve on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monteverde's local culture: visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (one of the original Quaker settler enterprises) for a tour and tasting (~$12 per person), then stop at a local organic coffee or chocolate tour to learn about sustainable Costa Rican agriculture (~$15–20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely final evening in Monteverde. Visit a local artisan market, pick up handmade pottery or woodwork souvenirs, and enjoy a relaxed dinner before preparing for tomorrow's transfer.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the eco-lodge — fresh local cheese (from Monteverde Cheese Factory), eggs, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Café in Santa Elena town center — 'casado' or fresh vegetable soup with homemade bread (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Cozy Monteverde restaurant with mountain views — grilled chicken in chimichurri with roasted vegetables and local wine or craft beer (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be busy at popular reserves — arrive at Curi-Cancha early (7:00 AM opening) for the best wildlife activity and fewer crowds. The cheese factory may have limited Sunday hours — verify in advance. Pack and prepare bags tonight for tomorrow's transfer to a new destination.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer from Monteverde to Arenal Volcano area (approx. 3 hours via scenic lake crossing or mountain road). The iconic Lake Arenal crossing by boat (15 min) followed by a short bus/taxi is the most scenic and recommended route. Arrive in La Fortuna/Arenal by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range eco-lodge with volcano views near La Fortuna. After settling in, visit the La Fortuna Waterfall (approx. 500 steps down to the base, ~$18 entrance). Swim in the cold, crystal-clear pool at the base of this stunning 70-meter cascade surrounded by lush rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Arenal hot springs. Choose a mid-range thermal spa option like Baldi Hot Springs or Ecotermales (~$35–45 per person) — natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by tropical gardens, perfect for relaxing muscles after the waterfall hike.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Monteverde eco-lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in La Fortuna town center upon arrival — 'casado' at a local soda or fresh fruit smoothie bowl (~$7–12)
meals.dinner: La Fortuna restaurant with Arenal Volcano views — try 'tilapia en salsa de maracuyá' (tilapia in passion fruit sauce) with rice and beans (~$14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The boat crossing on Lake Arenal is a highlight — try to sit on the right side of the boat for the best volcano views. The waterfall trail involves a steep descent and ascent — wear sturdy shoes and allow 1.5–2 hours round trip. Book hot springs in advance, especially for peak February season. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and sandals for the hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano National Park guided hike (7:00–10:30 AM, ~$30–45 per person with guide). Trek through old lava fields and primary rainforest on the volcano's flanks with a naturalist guide. Learn about the 1968 eruption history, spot wildlife like coatis, toucans, and leaf-cutter ants, and enjoy spectacular volcano views on clear mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Toro River (Class II–III rapids, approx. 3 hours, ~$55–75 per person). An exhilarating eco-adventure through lush rainforest canyon with excellent wildlife viewing from the river — look for kingfishers, caimans, and river otters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a well-earned rest. Browse the town's lively main street, visit a local supermarket for snacks, and enjoy a casual dinner before an early night.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your Arenal eco-lodge — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch included with most rafting tour operators — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Casual La Fortuna restaurant — 'chifrijo' (rice, beans, pork, and pico de gallo) or grilled beef with yuca and salad, with a local beer (~$10–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear quick-dry clothing and water shoes for rafting. All safety equipment is provided. The Balsa River (Class II) is suitable for families and beginners; the Toro River (Class III) offers more excitement — choose based on your comfort level. February's dry season means lower water levels on some rivers; confirm with operators the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Hanging Bridges walk in the Arenal area (Mistico or Arenal Hanging Bridges, ~$28–35 per person). Walk through primary rainforest on a series of suspension bridges at canopy level — spectacular views of the forest from above and excellent wildlife spotting including sloths, toucans, and morpho butterflies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Chocolate and coffee cultural tour at a local organic farm near La Fortuna (approx. 2 hours, ~$30–40 per person). Learn the entire process from cacao pod to chocolate bar and coffee cherry to espresso. Participate hands-on in processing and enjoy generous tastings of both.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back toward the Pacific coast or San José area (approx. 3–3.5 hours). Check into a mid-range hotel near the airport or in San José for a convenient final days' base. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal eco-lodge — last morning in the volcano region, enjoy it with views of Arenal
meals.lunch: Lunch included at the chocolate/coffee farm tour, or stop at a local soda en route (~$7–10)
meals.dinner: San José mid-range restaurant — try traditional 'olla de carne' or upscale Costa Rican fusion cuisine in the Barrio Escalante neighborhood (~$16–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If returning to the Aegean Bliss Resort for remaining nights, adjust the transfer destination accordingly. Barrio Escalante in San José is a vibrant culinary neighborhood worth exploring for dinner. Confirm your hotel booking near the airport or in San José in advance. Pack efficiently tonight as you'll be moving toward your final base.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Poás Volcano National Park (approx. 1.5 hours from San José, ~$15 entrance). Walk to the crater viewpoint of one of the world's largest active volcanic craters — on clear February mornings, the views are spectacular. Visit the nearby Botos Lagoon in a secondary cloud forest habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Doka Estate or Café Britt coffee plantation in the Central Valley on the way back to San José (approx. 1.5 hour tour, ~$22–30 per person). Tour the historic coffee plantation, learn about Costa Rica's 'golden bean' heritage, and enjoy a cupping session of premium single-origin coffees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to San José for a cultural evening. Visit the National Theater (Teatro Nacional) for a guided tour or evening performance if available (~$10–15 for tour, ~$20–40 for performance). Explore the historic downtown area around Plaza de la Cultura.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your San José hotel — standard continental or Costa Rican breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near Poás Volcano or at a local soda in the Central Valley — fresh strawberry jam and cream (the Poás region is famous for strawberries!) with a sandwich (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: San José restaurant in Barrio Escalante or Paseo Colón — try 'ceviche tico' (Costa Rican-style ceviche with lime and cilantro) and grilled meats (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Poás Volcano requires advance online reservations (timed entry slots) — book at least 3–5 days ahead at sinac.go.cr. The volcano is occasionally closed due to activity — check status the day before. Bring a warm layer as the crater rim sits at 2,700 m elevation. The National Theater tour is a cultural highlight not to miss — check their website for evening performance schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lankester Botanical Garden near Cartago (approx. 45 min from San José, ~$12 entrance). Home to one of the world's finest orchid collections with over 1,100 species. February is excellent for orchid blooms. Spend 2 hours wandering beautiful tropical gardens — a peaceful, photogenic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Irazú Volcano National Park (approx. 1 hour from Cartago, ~$15 entrance) — the highest volcano in Costa Rica at 3,432 m. Walk to the crater rim for views of the dramatic Diego de la Haya crater lake. On very clear days, you can see both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts simultaneously.
day_by_day.evening: Return to San José for a farewell dinner at one of the city's best mid-range restaurants. Reflect on the incredible 13-day journey through Costa Rica's diverse ecosystems. Do final souvenir shopping at a local artisan market or the Mercado Central.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in San José — enjoy a final proper Costa Rican gallo pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Picnic or café near Irazú Volcano — warm soup is welcome at 3,400 m elevation! Local vendors outside the park sell hot empanadas and coffee (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality San José restaurant — splurge slightly on a 'pargo entero frito' (whole fried red snapper) or filet mignon with chimichurri, with a bottle of Chilean wine (~$22–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Irazú is often shrouded in clouds by midday — arrive early for the best crater views. Bring very warm layers (temperatures near freezing at the summit) and rain gear. The Mercado Central in San José is a bustling indoor market great for last-minute gifts: local coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and handmade crafts at good prices. Pack your bags tonight for tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel. If time permits before checkout, take a final walk in a nearby park or visit the Museo Nacional de Costa Rica (National Museum, ~$9 entrance) in downtown San José for a fascinating overview of Costa Rican history, pre-Columbian artifacts, and natural history — located in a former fortress with a beautiful butterfly garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security). Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Costa Rican coffee, Lizano sauce, or Britt chocolates. Board your flight home with incredible memories of 13 days in one of the world's great eco-tourism destinations.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — 'Pura Vida!' as the Costa Ricans say.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor one last cup of Costa Rican coffee, considered among the world's finest
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café before departure — 'casado' one final time, or a light sandwich and fresh juice (~$10–15)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and adjust the morning schedule accordingly — allow at minimum 2.5 hours at the airport for international departures from SJO. Keep one souvenir bag as carry-on if you've purchased fragile items. Declare any food items (coffee, chocolate) at customs in your home country. Consider downloading your photos to cloud storage before departure. 'Pura Vida' — the pure life — Costa Rica's motto perfectly sums up this incredible 13-day journey through cloud forests, volcanoes, beaches, and wildlife.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges with breathtaking views of the forest below. A must-do eco-adventure that puts you eye-level with toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species including the great green macaw. Between July and October, witness nesting sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Jungle Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The hike concludes at a stunning Pacific Ocean beach, perfect for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk a series of hanging suspension bridges through primary rainforest in the shadow of the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting wildlife at every level of the forest canopy. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush jungle — the ultimate eco-adventure reward.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Guided Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' A full-day guided trek through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unparalleled chances to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their pristine natural habitat.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in a luxury SUV. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's ocean-view terrace, followed by a relaxed first dinner at the resort's signature restaurant to acclimate and unwind.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light snack or in-flight meal en route
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled pargo rojo (red snapper) caught locally, paired with a curated Costa Rican craft cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge upon arrival. Pack light for the next day's activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling or kayaking excursion along the coastline near the resort — explore coral reefs and spot tropical marine life including parrotfish, rays, and sea turtles in the warm Pacific waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beachfront yoga session arranged by the resort followed by a premium spa treatment — choose from a volcanic stone massage or a rainforest botanical body wrap at the resort's luxury spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront dinner under the stars — a bespoke candlelit table set on the sand with a personalized tasting menu crafted by the resort's head chef, featuring local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view terrace — tropical fruit platter, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch — ceviche trio, grilled lobster tacos, fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront tasting menu — 5-course meal featuring Costa Rican heritage ingredients: hearts of palm salad, plantain-crusted sea bass, chocolate-chili dessert with local Britt cacao

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to allow full recovery from travel. Book the spa treatment in advance through the concierge. Sunscreen and reef-safe products are recommended for marine activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private charter flight or luxury vehicle to Tortuguero National Park. Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through lush jungle canals on a private guided boat, spotting caimans, howler monkeys, toucans, green iguanas, and river otters in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the canal safari deeper into the park's network of waterways. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about Tortuguero's legendary nesting green sea turtles and ongoing conservation efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort. Relax with a sunset cocktail at the bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — overnight oats with tropical fruit, avocado toast, fresh coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort and enjoyed on the boat amid the jungle canals — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — slow-braised Costa Rican beef short rib with yuca purée, accompanied by a local Guanacaste wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Wear lightweight, neutral-colored, moisture-wicking clothing. Bring binoculars for wildlife spotting. Insect repellent is essential. Depart no later than 6:00 AM for maximum wildlife activity on the canals.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided birdwatching tour in the forests and wetlands surrounding the resort area — Costa Rica is home to over 900 bird species. Spot scarlet macaws, resplendent quetzals (if elevation permits), and dozens of hummingbird species with a certified ornithologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local premium sustainable coffee and chocolate farm for an immersive tasting tour. Learn the bean-to-bar and seed-to-cup process, and enjoy a curated tasting of single-origin chocolates and micro-lot coffees.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class with the resort's executive chef — learn to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes including gallo pinto, olla de carne, and tres leches cake, then enjoy your creations for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly baked croissants, local cheese board, tropical smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at the coffee and chocolate estate — fresh salads, local cheeses, artisan bread, and estate-grown herbal teas
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class, served in the resort's private dining room with curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Confirm birdwatching tour start time (recommended 5:30–6:00 AM for peak activity). Bring a camera with a telephoto lens. The cooking class typically runs 2–3 hours in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 2–3 hours depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Jungle Hike with a certified naturalist guide — spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two and three-toed sloths, squirrel monkeys, and vibrant poison dart frogs.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, relax on the pristine white-sand beaches within the national park — Manuel Antonio features some of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches accessible only through the park. Enjoy a private picnic lunch on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Sunset cocktails followed by a seafood-focused dinner celebrating the day's coastal adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — eggs any style, fresh fruit, Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on Manuel Antonio beach — chilled shrimp, avocado wraps, fresh fruit, artisan lemonade
meals.dinner: Resort's beachfront restaurant — whole grilled catch of the day with chimichurri, coconut rice, and patacones (fried plantains)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio has a daily visitor cap — ensure entrance tickets are pre-booked. The park opens at 7:00 AM; arrive early for best wildlife sightings. Bring biodegradable sunscreen and water shoes for the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day departure to the Arenal Volcano region via private luxury vehicle or charter flight. Upon arrival, begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience — walk a series of suspension bridges through primary old-growth rainforest with sweeping views of Arenal Volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Arenal experience with a visit to a premium private hot springs resort — soak in thermally heated natural mineral pools surrounded by lush tropical gardens, with views of the volcano.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury eco-lodge near Arenal for an overnight stay (pre-arranged as part of the itinerary). Enjoy a gourmet dinner at the lodge with volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast before departure — full tropical spread
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the hanging bridges park café or packed by your resort — grilled chicken wraps, tropical salad, fresh juice
meals.dinner: Arenal luxury eco-lodge restaurant — wood-fired Costa Rican cuisine, including local river trout, plantain soup, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: The drive from the Pacific coast to Arenal is approximately 3–4 hours. Depart by 7:00 AM. Pack an overnight bag for the Arenal stay. The hot springs are best enjoyed in the evening when the volcanic mist creates a magical atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk around the Arenal Volcano base with a naturalist — spot coatis, howler monkeys, toucans, and the iconic volcano in morning light. Optional kayaking or paddleboarding on Lake Arenal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Rest and refresh upon return. Optional resort pool time or spa session.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome-back dinner at the resort — celebrate the midpoint of the trip with a premium wine pairing dinner at the resort's fine dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast — farm-fresh eggs, local cheese, tropical fruits, artisan coffee
meals.lunch: En route stop at a highly rated roadside soda (traditional Costa Rican restaurant) — casado plate with rice, beans, plantains, and grilled meat
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — 4-course tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings: tuna tartare, cream of peach palm soup, beef tenderloin with chimichurri, passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer timing with the concierge. The drive back is approximately 3–4 hours. Consider a brief stop at a scenic viewpoint or artisan market en route.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horseback riding tour through coastal rainforest trails and along the beach — a quintessential Costa Rican experience offering stunning scenery and wildlife encounters from a unique vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local sustainable wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center — get up close with rescued sloths, toucans, monkeys, and other native species while learning about Costa Rica's world-leading conservation programs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sailing cruise along the coastline on a private catamaran — enjoy champagne, fresh ceviche, and tropical appetizers while watching the Pacific sunset, with dolphins often accompanying the boat.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast with local microgreens, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the wildlife rescue center's café or a nearby farm-to-table restaurant — grilled vegetables, local cheeses, artisan bread
meals.dinner: Return to resort for a romantic dinner — surf and turf featuring locally sourced lobster tail and grass-fed beef, with a curated cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the horseback riding and catamaran cruise in advance through the concierge. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for horseback riding. The sunset cruise typically departs 2 hours before sunset — confirm exact time with the operator.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day expedition to Corcovado National Park — depart early via private transfer or charter flight to the Osa Peninsula. Begin the Corcovado National Park Guided Rainforest Expedition with a certified naturalist guide. Trek through the most biologically diverse rainforest on Earth, spotting tapirs, scarlet macaws, peccaries, and possibly jaguars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition deeper into the park — explore pristine beaches within the park boundary, observe nesting sea birds, and visit freshwater swimming holes surrounded by primary rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort (or overnight at a luxury eco-lodge on the Osa Peninsula if preferred). Celebratory dinner after an extraordinary day in one of the world's last great wildernesses.

meals.breakfast: Very early resort breakfast before 5:00 AM departure — energy-packed options: granola, protein-rich eggs, strong local coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the resort, enjoyed in the rainforest — sandwiches, energy bars, tropical fruit, electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or Osa Peninsula luxury lodge — fresh jungle-to-table cuisine: heart of palm salad, grilled dorado, chocolate lava cake with local cacao

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits — ensure these are arranged by the concierge well in advance. This is the most physically demanding day of the trip; wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots. The expedition is 8–10 hours total including transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Optional gentle yoga or meditation class on the resort's beachfront deck led by a private instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full luxury spa afternoon — indulge in a 2-hour premium spa package including a coffee scrub (using local Costa Rican coffee), a hot stone massage, and a hydrating facial using native botanical ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfire experience arranged by the resort — a curated bonfire on the private beach with personalized cocktail service, live acoustic Costa Rican music, and a gourmet s'mores and dessert station.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast in bed or on your private suite terrace — continental spread with fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Resort beach club — lobster bisque, grilled fish tacos, fresh coconut sorbet
meals.dinner: Beachfire private dining — artisan charcuterie and cheese boards, grilled skewers, tropical desserts, premium rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest and recovery day after the intense Corcovado expedition. Encourage hydration and rest. Pre-book the spa package at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to the Monteverde Cloud Forest region (approximately 4–5 hours or 45-minute charter flight). Upon arrival, check into a luxury cloud forest lodge. Begin the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits, with cables spanning over 1km and platforms high above the forest canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided night walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve — discover the magical nocturnal world of the cloud forest, spotting glass frogs, kinkajous, sleeping birds, and bioluminescent fungi with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the cloud forest lodge with panoramic views of the misty forest canopy.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — full tropical spread
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the Monteverde lodge upon arrival — cloud forest-inspired cuisine: mushroom risotto, local trout, herbal teas
meals.dinner: Monteverde luxury lodge restaurant — elevated Costa Rican cuisine: chayote soup, braised lamb with local spices, tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde is significantly cooler than the coast — pack a light jacket and long pants. The zip-line tour requires closed-toe shoes. The night walk typically begins at 6:00 PM and lasts 2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — one of the most pristine cloud forest reserves in Central America, offering exceptional birdwatching including the resplendent quetzal. Visit the Orchid Garden and Butterfly Garden for close-up encounters with Monteverde's extraordinary biodiversity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive in the late afternoon and enjoy a final sunset swim in the ocean or resort infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner — the resort's most exclusive dining experience, arranged as a special send-off celebration with personalized menu, champagne toast, and a gift of local artisan products.

meals.breakfast: Cloud forest lodge breakfast — farm-fresh eggs, local cheeses, cloud forest honey, herbal teas and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: En route stop at a highly regarded restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, tropical salad
meals.dinner: Resort's signature farewell dinner — champagne reception, 6-course tasting menu celebrating the best of Costa Rican cuisine and ingredients, with paired wines and a personalized dessert

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Monteverde back to the resort is approximately 4–5 hours. Depart by 9:00 AM to arrive in time for a relaxed afternoon. Request the farewell dinner setup through the concierge in advance for maximum personalization.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the private beach — a quiet, reflective last morning in paradise. Optional early morning surf lesson or stand-up paddleboarding session for one last ocean adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort after a leisurely final breakfast. Private luxury transfer to the airport for departure. Stop at a premium artisan market or boutique en route to pick up high-quality Costa Rican souvenirs — single-origin coffee, artisan chocolate, handcrafted jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — carrying memories of 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and luxury.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort — the full spread: made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, pastries, specialty coffee, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge — club sandwich, tropical salad, fresh juice
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late checkout if your flight allows. Confirm private airport transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Allow extra time at the airport for souvenir shopping and duty-free. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs are legally certified — avoid purchasing products made from protected species.
